name: Unrehearsed
tagline: Anyone can get the laugh. You're after the second before it.
epigraph: One of the most familiar cocktails, inside ice. Nobody tastes it until the ice breaks.
glassware: rocks glass (about 300 ml), holding a shell of ordinary cloudy ice frozen in a plastic cup
language_row: Wren's Resonance on reading v5: ready. Sibling swap clean against the Stand-up (*Is It Just Me*: recognition; here surprise), the Wacky One (*For Kicks*: kept for life; here dropped once expected), the Surrealist (*The Other Berry*: "weird" never pinned on the guest), the Morale Booster and the Entertainer; *Off-Label* (repeat yourself), *Cold Water First* (the silence) and *No Accident* ("rather be misunderstood") all avoided. 4-grams clean over every pour; collisions reworded (Genie's opener, "in front of people", "with a joke and", "to see what you", "the person it's for", "and a twist of"). One "I"; the "he" in yours 2 is Joly (accepted). No "awkward", "weird", "molecular", no Kaufman, no hoax. ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/aviary-charles-joly.md`: Robert Simonson, *A Proper Drink* pp. 234–235 (In the Rock, "received… rather coolly at first", Joly's arrival "altered" the approach; "a bartender joke and a chat" is Simonson's narration); Mike Sula, *Chicago Reader*, 26 May 2011 (server cracks the ice; "subtler comic effect"; could seem "chilly, impersonal"); *Time Out Chicago*, 2014 (Joly: "lacked a sense of hospitality"; "Hugs, rum and rock"; "hospitality, the booze and a good time"); *PUNCH* 2017 (New York branch method, dossier only). Drink: Oxford OLD-FASHIONED pdf 1429; *Cocktail Codex* pp. 6, 109 (Zacapa's affinity with rye, aged in former whiskey barrels); Dave Arnold, *Liquid Intelligence* pdf 145 and pp. 78–79; Zacapa 23 at 40% (retailer pages, secondary). Room notes: `work/jester-explorer/`.
names_note: **Unrehearsed**, the room's pick (all three): the person's laugh, never the drink (Hester's condition: the 2011 drink took years of workshopping, *Proper* p. 234). Runner-up **Cold Open** (comedy term and ice at once), held back because it opens like *Cold Water First*. Also considered: *Just as Strange*, *The Second Before*, *Stay for the Chat*, *Cracked Open*.
open_items: **The rum swapped twice** (rounds 4 and 5, crossings). Tomás ruled it in once in round 6, for Zacapa's affinity with rye (*Codex* p. 109) and Joly's "Hugs, rum and rock", not to rescue the numbers (an all-rye version balances too, at 31.0% with more syrup and water). The no-rum y4 is kept in `work/jester-explorer/psychologist-alternatives.md`.

**The serve is ours, not the Aviary's.** In 2011 a server cracked the ice; here whoever made it cracks it at the table. The freezer-and-cup shell is Tomás's method, and the freezing time and small melt are his craft calls (unmeasured; *LI* pp. 78–79 says ice melts into a strong drink even at the same temperature).

**Zacapa 23 is named** because the affinity claim is about that bottle; the substitute (any aged Spanish-style rum, not spiced) doesn't inherit it. Never "23 years" (a blend of six to twenty-five). Its 40% is from retailer pages.

**Kept out on purpose:** the drink's name ("In the Rock"/"In the Rocks"), Simonson's rock/rocks pun, crediting Joly with "a joke and a chat", any cause for the 2012 change (Joly's predecessor left; "I like to think" only), "puzzled", "sealed", and "perhaps the finest".
**Strength:** 31.9% at serve; the rye must be about 40% (a 50% rye with a 46% rum goes over the band).
